title: Third Clash of the Week: China Fires Water Cannon at Philippine Vessel Carrying CNN Crew Near Scarborough Shoal
detail: A China Coast Guard vessel fired a water cannon at a Philippine vessel carrying a CNN news crew near Scarborough Shoal on July 24, 2026 — the third confrontation between China and the Philippines in a single week, following the July 20 baton incident at Second Thomas Shoal and the July 23 water cannon incident blocking a fisher resupply mission. The Philippine government said the string of incidents amounted to "repeated aggressive, unprofessional and illegal" actions by China. China Coast Guard said it "drove away" Philippine vessels it accused of "intruding" into waters near the shoal. The clashes prompted the US, Japan and the Philippines to conduct joint maritime drills in the South China Sea through July 25.

media.caption: Chinese ship shoots water cannon at Philippine vessel with CNN crew on board near Scarborough Shoal

title: 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting Closes in Manila With Pledge to Finalize South China Sea Code of Conduct by Year-End
detail: The 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, held in Manila July 18-24, 2026 under a cloud of fresh China-Philippines clashes, closed with ministers voicing "sustained positive momentum" in Code of Conduct (COC) negotiations and reaffirming a target to conclude the COC by the end of 2026, with a planned finalization at the 49th ASEAN Summit in November. China's ambassador Jing Quan said Beijing's willingness to "finish the (code) talks at the end of this year has not changed," clarifying the COC would set operational "rules of engagement" rather than resolve territorial disputes. Malaysian Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan expressed optimism about a November conclusion. The Philippines was unable to forge a unified ASEAN bloc statement condemning the week's clashes, as the meetings again exposed divisions within the ten-member bloc over how forcefully to address Chinese assertiveness in the South China Sea.

sources.name: Friends of Socialist China / China-ASEAN FMM coverage

media.caption: ASEAN foreign ministers close 59th AMM in Manila, pledge to finalize South China Sea Code of Conduct by year-end

title: Australia Commits Additional AUD 4.6 Billion to Expand Osborne Submarine Shipyard Under AUKUS
detail: Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles announced on July 24, 2026 an additional AUD 4.6 billion (USD 3.2 billion) investment to expand infrastructure and workforce training at the Osborne shipyard in South Australia, as part of Australia's implementation of the AUKUS nuclear-powered submarine partnership with the US and UK. The new facility will expand to roughly ten times the current shipyard's size to build and sustain Australia's future SSN-AUKUS boats. Marles called it "another important step in building the sovereign capability" Australia needs for submarine operations amid intensifying Indo-Pacific competition, including in the South China Sea.

media.caption: Australia commits AUD 4.6 billion to expand the Osborne submarine shipyard under AUKUS
